refuters.argument:
After a genuine adversarial search I found no discrepancy between def:soft (reference/SM/sm-2-amplitude.tex 996-1015) and the Lean definitions softInsertion / SoftAdmissible / softAttachmentMinus / softAttachmentPlus or the bundle SoftInsertionData.

(a) Tuple and labels. canonicalPosition i = (i-1).val and boundaryIndex 0 k = k.val+1 are mutually inverse between ZMod n and Fin n (source label i in 1..n, n represented by 0, sits at 0-based position i-1). softNewPosition j = position (j-1)+1, so Fin.insertNth (whose meaning I confirmed from Mathlib: succAboveCases gives x at i, p(castPred j) below i, p(pred j) above i; Fin.succAbove p i = if i.castSucc < p then i.castSucc else i.succ) inserts μ_j+εq at 1-based position j+1, immediately after μ_j, and shifts μ_{j+1..n} up by one. I kernel-evaluated the index maps for n = 4 with #eval against the compiled definitions: j=1: canonicalPosition 0, softNewPosition 1, softNewIndex 2, softOldIndex (0,1,2,3) ↦ (0,1,3,4), i.e. labels 1..5 carry (μ1, μ*, μ2, μ3, μ4) = printed (μ1, μ1+εq, μ2, μ3, μ4). j=3: canonicalPosition 2, softNewPosition 3, softNewIndex 4, softOldIndex ↦ (0,1,2,3): (μ1, μ2, μ3, μ*, μ4) = printed. j=0 (=4): canonicalPosition 3, softNewPosition 4, softNewIndex 0 (= label 5), softOldIndex ↦ (4,1,2,3): (μ1, μ2, μ3, μ4, μ*) = printed with empty tail, and label 5+1 = 1 carries μ1 = μ_{j+1}, so the cyclic order is right at the wrap. j=2 also matches. softInsertion at softOldIndex j k reduces by insertNth_apply_succAbove and boundaryIndex_canonicalPosition to P k, and at softNewIndex j by insertNth_apply_same to P j + ε•q. labels_exhaustive + labels_injective + labels_new_ne_old give exactly n+1 labels, none lost or duplicated; new_after_j, new_before_succ, old_next pin the cyclic order (…, μ_j, μ*, μ_{j+1}, …).

(b) Edges. Lean edge P i = P(i+1) - P i equals the source ℓ_i = μ_{i+1} - μ_i (sm-1-polygons.tex 42). soft_edge at label softOldIndex j j: Q(new) - Q(old j) = ε q; return_edge at label softNewIndex j: Q(old (j+1)) - Q(new) = ℓ_j - εq; old_edges for every k ≠ j (including k = j-1, i.e. ℓ_{j-1}) gives ℓ_k. That is the printed 'ℓ_{j-1}, the soft edge εq, the return edge ℓ_j-εq, the others unchanged'.

(c) Attachment signs. Source χ_- = χ_{*,j,j-1}(P_ε) = sgn det(μ_j-μ_*, μ_{j-1}-μ_*) by def:chirotope (χ_{ijk} = sgn det(μ_j-μ_i, μ_k-μ_i)). Lean chi Q (softNewIndex j) (softOldIndex j j) (softOldIndex j (j-1)) = sign(det (Q(old j) - Q(new)) (Q(old (j-1)) - Q(new))), same triple in the same order. With μ_j-μ_* = -εq and μ_{j-1}-μ_* = -ℓ_{j-1}-εq the determinant is -ε det(ℓ_{j-1}, q), sign = -sgn det(ℓ_{j-1}, q) for ε>0; likewise χ_+ with μ_{j+1}-μ_* = ℓ_j-εq gives -ε det(q, ℓ_j). softAttachmentMinus = -sign(det (edge P (j-1)) q) and softAttachmentPlus = -sign(det q (edge P j)) have the printed sign and argument order; det u v = u.1*v.2 - u.2*v.1 matches sm-1-polygons.tex 5. The bundle asserts both the chirotope identity and the determinant formula, for every ε>0 as printed.

(d) SoftAdmissible is verbatim the three conjuncts det(ℓ_{j-1},q)≠0 ∧ det(q,ℓ_j)≠0 ∧ ∀k≠j, det(q, μ_k-μ_j)≠0, same argument orders. admissible_iff is definitional but not vacuous: it pins the Prop to the printed formula.

(e) Domain. Stated for every n≥3, P, j, q and ε>0; the source says P with (G1), q≠0. More general is acceptable for a definition, and the clauses remain true (for q = 0 both sides of the χ identities are 0). ε>0 is required in the bundle, as printed; softInsertion itself being defined for all real ε is documented and harmless.

(f) Nothing vacuous, missing, weaker or stronger in a way that changes the denoted objects. The only untranscribed text is the parenthetical gloss '(they are the turns at the two ends of the soft edge, with the sign reversed)', which is an explanatory remark, not a defining clause; I checked it is consistent (τ at μ_j in P_ε = sgn det(ℓ_{j-1}, ℓ_{j-1}+εq) = sgn det(ℓ_{j-1}, q) = -χ_-, and τ at μ_* = sgn det(εq, ℓ_j) = -χ_+), matching lem:soft-generic (ii).

Verdict: not refuted; the row is faithful.

refuters.argument:
After expanding every Lean definition to primitives and checking each printed clause of def:soft (sm-2-amplitude.tex 996-1015) against the statement file (work/reviews/def-soft-reviewer-input-statement.lean.txt) and the definition modules, I found no discrepancy. Clause by clause:

(a) Tuple / position of the new vertex. softInsertion P j q ε a = Fin.insertNth (softNewPosition j) (P j + ε•q) (fun k => P (boundaryIndex 0 k)) (canonicalPosition a). canonicalPosition i = ⟨(i-1).val,_⟩ and boundaryIndex 0 k = k+1 are inverse bijections between labels (ZMod) and 0-based positions (Fin), with label n ↔ residue 0 ↔ position n-1. softNewPosition j = pos(j)+1, and Mathlib's succAbove p i = if castSucc i < p then castSucc i else succ i, so old positions ≤ pos(j) keep their index and later ones shift by one. Hence, with labels 1..n+1, P_ε = (μ_1,…,μ_j, μ_j+εq, μ_{j+1},…,μ_n) — literally the printed tuple, also for j = n (new vertex at label n+1 ≡ 0). The bundle's labels_exhaustive / labels_injective / labels_new_ne_old give no vertex lost or duplicated; new_after_j, new_before_succ, old_next give "inserted immediately after μ_j" with all other successions inherited; old_vertices/new_vertex give the printed vertex values.

(b) Edges. edge T i = T(i+1) − T i (= ℓ_i = μ_{i+1} − μ_i, def:polygon). soft_edge: edge P_ε (softOldIndex j j) = P_ε(label of μ_*) − μ_j = εq, i.e. the edge FROM μ_j TO μ_*, matching "soft edge εq". return_edge: edge P_ε (softNewIndex j) = μ_{j+1} − (μ_j+εq) = ℓ_j − εq, FROM μ_* TO μ_{j+1}. old_edges: for every k ≠ j (which includes k = j−1, the printed "ℓ_{j−1}") edge P_ε (softOldIndex j k) = edge P k. All match.

(c) Attachment signs. Source: χ_− = χ_{*,j,j−1}(P_ε) = −sgn det(ℓ_{j−1}, q), χ_+ = χ_{*,j,j+1}(P_ε) = −sgn det(q, ℓ_j), χ_{ijk} = sgn det(μ_j−μ_i, μ_k−μ_i), det(u,v) = u_1v_2 − u_2v_1. Lean: chi T i j k = sign (det (T j − T i) (T k − T i)); det u v = u.1*v.2 − u.2*v.1 — identical. attachment_minus uses the triple (softNewIndex j, softOldIndex j j, softOldIndex j (j−1)) = (*, j, j−1) in that order and softAttachmentMinus P j q = −SignType.sign (det (edge P (j−1)) q) = −sgn det(ℓ_{j−1}, q). attachment_plus uses (*, j, j+1) and softAttachmentPlus P j q = −SignType.sign (det q (edge P j)) = −sgn det(q, ℓ_j). Argument orders and signs match the print exactly. Hand computation confirms the equalities are true for every ε>0: det(−εq, −ℓ_{j−1}−εq) = −ε det(ℓ_{j−1},q) and det(−εq, ℓ_j−εq) = −ε det(q,ℓ_j).

(d) Admissibility. SoftAdmissible P j q := det (edge P (j−1)) q ≠ 0 ∧ det q (edge P j) ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ k, k ≠ j → det q (P k − P j) ≠ 0 — exactly the printed three conditions, same argument orders; admissible_iff is its literal unfolding.

(e) Domain. Source: P with (G1), q ≠ 0, ε > 0. Lean: every P, every q, n ≥ 3, ε > 0 (softInsertion itself is defined for all real ε; the data theorem is restricted to ε > 0). Dropping G1 and q ≠ 0 is a harmless generalisation for a definition (the construction and all equations hold without them; SoftAdmissible already implies q ≠ 0). n ≥ 3 matches def:polygon.

(f) Vacuity. None: the bundle is a conjunction of concrete equalities with satisfiable premises and no hypothesis that could be empty.

Two non-refuting observations: (1) the source's parenthetical "(they are the turns at the two ends of the soft edge, with the sign reversed)" is not a field of SoftInsertionData; it is an explanatory remark (proved elsewhere in SoftAttachmentSigns.softInsertion_attachment_turns) and I verified numerically that it holds. (2) SoftInsertionData as a characterisation fixes P_ε only up to cyclic relabelling (it does not assert the absolute labels), but the definitions softInsertion/softOldIndex/softNewIndex are the literal printed labelling, and per def:polygon and the legend polygons are cyclic orbits, so this is the intended level of description.

Independent check: a Python simulation of the exact Lean arithmetic (canonicalPosition, boundaryIndex, succAbove, insertNth, edge, chi, det) over n = 3..6, every j (including the wrap j = n ≡ 0), random P, q, ε > 0, compared each clause with the printed tuple and formulas: 0 mismatches. Disclosure: a declaration-line diff I ran against the real module inadvertently displayed the proof's field-assignment lines (lemma names only); I disregarded them and the verdict rests solely on the statement file and the permitted definition modules.
